To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

self-locking of modes is possible if the following conditions are met: the gain curve has a sufficiently large curvature, the laser cavity is sufficiently long (or equivalently, the round-trip time is sufficiently long), the laser gain medium is sufficiently long (and the gain curve sufficiently flat) so as to permit the buildup of a sufficiently strong population difference, and the gain is not saturated by the field.
self-locking is possible in a laser with a homogeneous line, and that the self-locking condition depends on the ratio of the cavity roundtrip time to the lifetime of the upper laser level.

the self-locking of modes in a ring gas laser or in a solid-state laser is possible if the following conditions are satisfied: (1) the laser has a large enough gain and a large enough loss; (2) the loss has a large enough dependence on the frequency; and (3) the laser has an appropriate feedback mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction of a high power laser beam with the atmosphere.

the study of the interaction between light waves in nonlinear optical media, and the application of the results of this study to the development of new devices for the generation of short light pulses.
the study of the properties of the modes of laser resonators and of the dynamics of the laser field under modelocked conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self‐locking is a phenomenon which can occur in lasers of any kind.
the self-locking of modes of a laser with homogeneous line broadening is a very complex phenomenon.
, for a laser with a homogeneously broadening line, there is no self-locking of modes if the laser is operated in the single-mode region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modelocked pulses are of the same order of magnitude as the laser pulses.
the laser modes are selflocked when the gain is sufficiently large and when the laser is sufficiently short.
we have developed a model for the mode locking in ring lasers and have calculated the field pulses under mode locked conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conditions for mode locking in a laser are very sensitive to the parameters of the active medium.
the self- locking of the laser modes is a nonlinear effect that depends on the shape of the field pulse and the shape of the pump pulse.
the self-locking conditions are more restrictive than the conditions for self-mode locking.
